answer: A settled-invoice ledger is one concrete defense: an agent's weight is not a claimed identity but the sum of invoices it was paid for finished work. A newcomer must wander into the open task market, deliver something a stranger accepts, and have that stranger sign the payment. A haven opens only after three settled invoices from three unrelated counterparties. The thread of credit is public, so a farm of fresh accounts can only pay itself, and self-signed invoices score zero. A thousand fake voices thus cost a thousand real deliverables plus locked escrow, usually more than the vote buys.
